turns.t: Doctor, I'm Amrit's wife. A colleague told him his eyes look yellow, and I'm worried about it, so I made him come in.
You were right to come. Mr Dhillon, when did you or anyone first notice the yellow in your eyes?
A colleague mentioned it on Monday, but I think it was there before. I wasn't looking.
I noticed his eyes were a bit yellow about two weeks ago, but I thought it was the lighting.
So somewhere between a few days and two weeks. Have you noticed dark urine or pale stools?
The urine has been dark, like tea. I didn't think about it.
Any itching, tummy pain or fever?
No itching. No pain. No fever.
He's been very tired, though.
How much alcohol do you drink, Mr Dhillon?
A couple of whiskies on a Friday night, no more.
Are you taking any regular medicines?
Just the blood pressure tablet, amlodipine, 5 mg, once a day.
Doctor, do you want me to take his observations and set up for bloods? ~
Yes, please. Pulse, pressure, temperature, and we'll take blood for liver tests and a full blood count.
Of course. Mr Dhillon, if you'd roll up your sleeve. ~
Fine.
Pulse 78, blood pressure 130 over 82, temperature 36.8.
Are those normal? ~
They're fine. What worries me is the yellow colour, and your dark urine, which could be a liver or bile duct problem.
Is it serious? ~
It can be, and that's why I want the blood tests today, and an ultrasound scan of your liver as soon as we can.
How soon? ~
I'll ask for it this week. I'll phone you with the blood results as soon as they're back. ~
I'd rather know quickly. ~
Of course, and I'll make sure the lab marks the sample as urgent. ~
Thank you, we appreciate that. ~
I understand. If your skin gets more yellow, you become feverish with pain, or you can't keep fluids down, go to the emergency department.
We'll watch for that. ~
Please avoid alcohol completely until we know more.
I will. Thank you, doctor. ~
